messages:
IncidentBot: Pager: SEV-2 - elevated error rates + routing churn for inference requests in eu-west and us-east regions. Symptoms: 502s from edge, repeated fallback to default model variant, latency spikes. Impact: some customers seeing failed requests and request loops. Runbook: https://runbooks/redwood/incidents/routing-fallback

Alex Chen: seeing this on dashboards too. spike started ~ 10:12 UTC, routing logs show repeated 302->fallback->302 loops to the same endpoint.

Maria Gomez: looks like edge DNS records for several POPs have stale A records pointing at decommissioned LB IPs. health-checks failing -> smart-routing policy marks region unhealthy -> fallback to another region which also has stale record -> oscillation.

Tilly (SRE): @Alex can you paste the last lines of the smart-router log for a single request id? need to confirm variant selection.

Alex Chen: pasted below:
```
[2026-03-15T10:13:02Z] req=abcd1234 route=smart-router selected_candidate=eu-west-1:variant-quant-small score=0.74
[2026-03-15T10:13:02Z] req=abcd1234 connect_failure=EHOSTUNREACH -> fallback to us-east-1:variant-prod
[2026-03-15T10:13:03Z] req=abcd1234 connect_failure=EHOSTUNREACH fallback_attempts=3 routing_decision=retry-same-policy
```

Alex Chen: note the selected_candidate is a quantized small variant (variant-quant-small) even though the policy should prefer prod variants for paid tenants. implies policy config drift.

Nikhil (OpsLead): Paging oncall to revert the recent routing policy change that introduced 'prefer-cheap-variants' rule. Maria, can you confirm recent deploys?

Maria Gomez: confirmed — there was a consumer-facing change 10:05 UTC that added a cost-aware policy as an experimental rollout. It mistakenly had a global scope instead of canary.

Tilly (SRE): mitigation plan (live):
1) disable prefer-cheap-variants flag in smart-router config (hotfix)
2) push TTL flush to Cloud DNS for affected zones (eu-west/us-east POPs)
3) temporarily increase probe frequency and set aggressive fail-open to avoid oscillation
4) notify customers and CS for impacted tenants

IncidentBot: Action taken: feature-flag 'prefer-cheap-variants' disabled by Nikhil at 10:22 UTC.

Alex Chen: after disabling flag, routing choices reverted to prod variants, but still seeing connection attempts to stale LB IPs.

Maria Gomez: Cloud DNS team reports incremental propagation delays; some edge caches (ISP-level) still hold old records. We'll request an emergency purge and lower TTL. Command I ran: `gcloud dns record-sets transaction start && gcloud dns record-sets transaction remove --name "pop-eu.example." --type A --ttl 300 <old-ip> --zone redwood-edge && gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute`

Tilly (SRE): While DNS propagates, we should reduce retry attempts and increase circuit-breaker thresholds to avoid retry storms. Alex, can you patch the client-facing LB health-check bypass for 15m?

Alex Chen: patch deployed: reduced retries from 5->2, sticky-session TTL relaxed. Logs show 50% reduction in repeated attempts.

Priya (CS): rolling customer notice to impacted tenants now. Template: "We're investigating increased failures to endpoints in eu-west/us-east; engineering applying mitigations; you may see increased latency or 502s for short window."

Nikhil (OpsLead): also opened vendor ticket with CDN provider — asking to purge POP caches and confirm propagation. Ticket #CDN-9981.

Maria Gomez: quick root cause hypothesis: accidental global rollout of a cost-aware routing flag combined with stale edge DNS records created a positive feedback loop: router marked POPs unhealthy -> routed traffic elsewhere -> other POPs overloaded -> fallbacks retried to original stale endpoints -> oscillation. Two independent failures combined into a loop.

Tilly (SRE): current status at 10:45 UTC: routing policy reverted, DNS change executed, CDN purge in progress, retries throttled. Error rate down from peak 12% -> 3%. Still monitoring for residual 502s. Postmortem owners: Maria (policy), Tilly (SRE), Alex (routing infra), Priya (customer comms).

Alex Chen: temporarily re-routed traffic for a small subset of enterprise customers to dedicated capacity to prevent impact while we finish cleanup. Added log marker `incident/1769456789` for correlation.

IncidentBot: On-call handoff scheduled: Tilly handing to Nikhil for next 2h monitoring window at 11:00 UTC.

Priya (CS): I've logged all affected tenants and contact points. Will follow up with a status email once 100% of POPs report healthy.

Tilly (SRE): next steps for postmortem:
- timeline reconstruction (Maria/Alex)
- reproduce policy rollout gating bug in staging (Maria)
- add guardrail to prevent global scope flags (code + deploy pipeline) (Alex)
- reduce default edge TTLs and implement emergency purge playbook with CDN (Ops)
- automated detection: add metric for routing oscillation (SRE)

Alex Chen: closing loop — steady state at 11:08 UTC, error rate ~0.8% and falling. Will keep thread open until 12:00 UTC then move to postmortem channel. :thumbsup:
